title: Sertoli-Leydig Cell Tumors, Gynandroblastoma & DICER1 Mutations
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumours 5e
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Ovarian Cancer (2024)

steps.say: Sertoli Leydig cell tumors represent uncommon sex cord stromal neoplasms characterized by androgen production. Clinical presentation features progressive defeminization followed by frank virilization.
steps.tx: **Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor** (**androblastoma**) represents <**0.5** percent of ovarian neoplasms, presenting with **progressive virilization** in young women (**median age 25** years, age **25** to **30**s). Striking clinical features include severe **clitoromegaly**, voice deepening, and hirsutism presenting in **30** to **50** percent of patients.

steps.say: Molecular discovery has linked the pathogenesis of Sertoli Leydig tumors to specific microRNA processing machinery defects. Somatic mutations cluster in the endoribonuclease domain of DICER1.
steps.tx: Pathognomonic **DICER1 mutation** in the **RNase IIIb domain** (codons E**1705**, D**1709**, G**1809**, or D**1810** in the **1**800 region) creates a severe **microRNA processing defect** in **>60% frequency** (**60** percent) of moderately and poorly differentiated SLCTs, disrupting oncogene silencing and driving dysregulated stromal cellular growth.

nodes.label: Acquire somatic hotspot mutation in DICER1 RNase IIIb domain
Impair cleavage of 5p-strand microRNAs from precursor hairpins
Promote dedifferentiation and sarcomatoid / heterologous SLCT growth

steps.say: Inherited germline variants in the DICER1 gene produce a broad pleiotropic hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome. Patients require screening for multi organ tumors throughout life.
steps.tx: Germline DICER**1** mutations cause the familial **DICER1 syndrome**, an autosomal dominant cancer syndrome predisposing to pediatric **pleuropulmonary blastoma**, **cystic nephroma**, differentiated thyroid carcinoma, and **pituitary blastoma**, requiring comprehensive multi-organ surveillance across the lifespan of affected patients and their families to detect tumors early.

rows: Chest CT; high risk of malignant lung sarcoma
Renal ultrasound; benign multilocular cystic mass
Thyroid palpation and annual ultrasound surveillance

steps.say: Biochemical evaluation of virilizing syndromes requires precise discrimination between adrenal and ovarian androgen sources. Markedly elevated testosterone in the presence of normal dehydroepiandrosterone confirms an ovarian lesion.
steps.tx: Marked **serum testosterone >200 ng/dL** (>**200** ng/dL, or >**7** nmol/L) paired with **normal DHEAS** provides crucial diagnostic discrimination for **ovarian vs adrenal virilization**, definitively establishing an androgen-secreting ovarian tumor rather than an adrenal cortical neoplasm or severe polycystic ovarian syndrome.

left.title: Ovarian Virilizing SLCT
points: Markedly elevated serum total testosterone (>200 ng/dL)
Unilateral solid ovarian mass on high-resolution pelvic ultrasound

right.title: Adrenal Androgen-Secreting Neoplasm
points: Variable or modest elevation of serum testosterone
Adrenal mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT / MRI

steps.say: Histological differentiation dictates clinical behavior and guides adjuvant therapeutic decision making. Well differentiated tumors follow an indolent benign course while poorly differentiated tumors behave aggressively.
steps.tx: The **Meyer classification** stratifies SLCT into well, intermediate, and poorly differentiated forms. Adverse histopathologic features include **retiform architecture** mimicking rete testis and presence of **heterologous elements** (such as gastrointestinal mucinous glands, cartilage, or aggressive **rhabdomyosarcoma stroma**), which herald higher metastatic recurrence risks.

rows: Hollow tubules lined by uniform Sertoli cells; interstitial Leydig cells
Benign clinical behavior (<1% recurrence); surgery curative
Lobular masses, primitive tubules, variable Leydig cell stroma
Sheets of sarcomatoid spindle cells; rudimentary cords
Aggressive behavior (~60% recurrence); requires adjuvant BEP
Mucinous glands, rhabdomyosarcoma, or anastomosing slit-like channels
Higher recurrence rate and resistance to standard chemotherapy

steps.say: Surgical resection restricted to the involved ovary cures encapsulated well differentiated tumors in young women. Systemic chemotherapy is indicated for high grade or advanced disease.
steps.tx: Encapsulated **stage IA well-differentiated USO** (unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy) is curative alone in young women. Conversely, **poorly differentiated BEP chemo** (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) or Stage **1**, **2**, or **4** disease with **heterologous elements adjuvant therapy** is mandatory to prevent rapid intra-abdominal recurrence.

nodes.label: Perform unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with preservation of uterus and opposite ovary
Review histological grade, presence of heterologous elements, and capsular rupture
Stage IA well-differentiated: observation only (excellent prognosis)
Moderately/poorly differentiated or Stage IC+: administer 3-4 cycles of BEP

steps.say: Gynandroblastoma is an exceedingly rare sex cord stromal neoplasm displaying mixed cellular lineages. Both male and female phenotypes are intimately admixed within the tumor.
steps.tx: Rare **gynandroblastoma** represents a distinctive **biphasic sex cord** neoplasm displaying **coexisting granulosa and Sertoli-Leydig** elements (each component comprising at least 10 percent of the tumor mass), manifesting clinically with alternating estrogenic endometrial bleeding and progressive hyperandrogenic virilizing symptoms in reproductive-age females.

vis.caption: High-grade serous carcinoma STIC lesions confirming fallopian tube origin. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Steroid cell tumors not otherwise specified represent pure androgen producing ovarian neoplasms. Tumor cells are packed with abundant intracytoplasmic lipid droplets.
steps.tx: **Steroid cell tumor NOS** represents a pure virilizing sex cord neoplasm. Key **malignancy predictors** on histological assessment include tumor **diameter >7 cm** (**7** cm), presence of necrosis, and high mitotic rate of **>=2-3 mitoses per 10 HPF** (**2** to **3** mitoses per **10** high-power fields), which predict malignant metastatic behavior.
